# Independent audit of the unequal-density payment

Audited Section4 of
`candidate a972493c7a264f4e`.
Result: PASS, including its pure-integer-direction bound. I also checked
the full-body transport inputs in Section1 against the direct coupling.

For unequal volumes the conditional diagonal product is b/a. Expanding
product(1+t_i) by subset size and applying AM–GM gives the stated
midpoint Jacobian lower bound v_*/a, with correct endpoint subset cases.
Thus eta=a Law(midpoint) has density at most theta=a/v_* and has the
actual weighted endpoint marginals 1_A and (a/b)1_B. Its mass, mean and
closed affine-offset cap inequality are exact.

The rescaling eta'=eta/theta changes neither the actual centroid law
1_K+2eta nor its support. After |K|=1, eta' has mass alpha<=1 because
k>=v_*, and theta alpha=a/k. The cap-root Jensen/rearrangement computation
with coefficient2theta gives exactly

    phi(U)+2theta phi(Q)+2theta phi(E)>=2theta/(d+1).

The same three Fenchel multipliers contribute D_theta/d, so

    D_theta<=A_d+theta X_d,
    X_d=1+A_d/3-epsilon_d.

Rewriting this bound leaves the nonnegative explicit reserve
C=(1-theta)A_d/3+theta epsilon_d. The exact mass identity is
(1+theta alpha)/s=U+theta Q+theta E-theta, which yields

    s+theta r>=(3/(4A_d))[1+theta alpha+C s].

Jensen before rearrangement gives
s>=Gamma_d/(1+2theta alpha)^d. Substitution and rescaling by k produce
precisely equation(9), including its factorGamma_d squared, factor k,
and denominator(1+2a/k)^d. The replacement of s by this lower bound
has the correct direction because C>0. This is the original captured
mass, not the smaller coupling's total mass.

For pure integer caps, X_d>=1 follows by keeping the linear binomial
term in (1+1/(2d))^(d+1) and dropping only the nonnegative other power.
Thus epsilon_d<=A_d/3, whence C<=A_d/3. The additional term is at most
Gamma_d k/4. Adding it to the first term gives at most
Gamma_d k+(3/4)Gamma_d a<k+a. This proves the claimed pure-direction
case without invoking a continuous trace or losing the boundary fiber.

The fixed-b,k limit of the displayed bound as a tends to zero is exactly
Gamma_d k: theta tends to zero and the denominator tends to one. The
source correctly limits this assertion to the bound, without claiming
that an unspecified extremal body or selected point converges.

No defect or repair is identified. The resulting bound remains a
finite-parameter conditional inequality at the explicitly defined
middle point, not a resolution of arbitrary endpoint imbalance or OC.
